narrative.overview:
The polyrouter dashboard is an operator's switchboard. Every request comes in at one point and leaves along one route, and the board's job is to show which route was lit and why. The brand mark sums it up at 20px: one source node fans out to three routes, and one route is lit in Ink Indigo while the other two stay grey. The system repeats that grammar wherever traffic is explained. Above all, it shapes the **Route Trace**, the signature component that draws a request's real path through the router.

Everything else stays quiet so the lit route can be read. Near-white panels sit on a flat board divided by 1px hairlines, and greys carry the structure. Indigo is spent only on what is active, selected or focused (The Indigo Budget Rule). Figures are honest before they are pretty. Every number is either exact or says what it is instead: estimated, unpriced, pending, stale or reserved (see *Figures and their states*). Density is compact because operators scan rather than read, and type grows only where a number is the point.

Controls are crisp and tactile. They are small and exact, and they share one height family. Every state (hover, pressed, selected, focus, busy, invalid) is shown as a tone, border or label change, never as lift or glow. On a first visit the theme follows the operating system. Dark mode mirrors every token and drops every shadow.

**How this file relates to the code.** DESIGN.md is the target: it describes what the dashboard should ship next, not only what ships today. Where target and code differ, the **As-built delta** table below names the gap and the OpenSpec change that closes it. Until that change lands, two things stay authoritative: the as-built value in `packages/frontend/src/styles.css` (for code) and the locked axes in `STYLESEED.md`. Each implementing change updates `STYLESEED.md`, `styles.css` and the contract tests together, then removes its rows from the delta.
keyCharacteristics: One brand hue, spent deliberately. Each view gets one indigo-filled control and one indigo data series. Washes, rings and indigo text mark state.
The Route Trace draws a request's path in the brand mark's grammar.
Honest figures: each state has one treatment, and the state is always named in words.
Flat surfaces. Hairlines separate them. Shadows are faint in light mode and absent in dark mode.
One control-height family (24 / 32px, and 44px under a coarse pointer) and five type sizes (11 / 12 / 13 / 15 / 26px).
Geist for words and numbers (numbers use tabular figures). Geist Mono for identifiers only.
Snap motion, and only state moves: the Live lamp blinks once per event, and the only loops are in-progress pulses and skeletons.

rules.name: The Indigo-Text Rule
rules.body: Text is never set in `--accent`. Indigo text, labels and icons use `accent-deep`, which reaches 5.86:1 or better in light mode and 4.72:1 or better in dark on every neutral surface (panel, canvas, chip, hover, wash). It never sits on a status wash, where dark Amber Wash drops it to 4.47:1. Raw accent text fails in dark mode (3.70:1) and on light washes (4.32:1).

rules.name: The 3:1 Edge Rule
rules.body: Anything whose edge *is* the affordance draws that edge in Control Edge: an empty field, a checkbox, an off switch. A state is shown by a change in shape, border or weight that clears 3:1, never by a tint alone. The selected wash is only 1.07–1.16:1 against its surroundings, so it never carries the state by itself.

rules.name: The Indigo Budget Rule
rules.body: Indigo is spent, not sprinkled. Each view gets: - **One indigo-filled control:** the primary action. Every other action is a neutral button, and switches are Ink. - **One indigo data series:** the view's focal measure. Examples: the Pipeline's bars, the Limits spend line, the request mix's two intensities, the Route Trace's lit branch. Every other series is Ink or Ink 3, told apart by dash pattern and direct labels. - **State marks without limit:** the focus ring, the focused input border and the caret; Deep Ink text and hover edges (links, selected labels, ghost and endpoint-chip hover); the Selected wash; and `accent-color` on a checked native checkbox or radio. These mark state, so they don't count against the budget. - **Identity:** the brand mark's lit route. It is the product's signature, not spend. A docked panel and the page beside it count as one view. Running dots, hover fills, icon chips and decorative accents are never indigo. A second accent hue breaks the board.

rules.name: The Status-Speaks Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red mean state, with one exception: red also marks an action that destroys data, abandons in-flight work, or cuts off access (Delete, Remove, Purge, Disable, Cancel batch). Every status color appears beside words that name the state. Never encode status by color alone, and never set small status text in the fill variant on a light surface.

rules.name: The No-Rainbow Rule
rules.body: Never give each card, series or category its own hue. Identity is carried by text. A categorical palette may arrive only through an explicit change to the `STYLESEED.md` lock (`+categorical`), not one surface at a time.

rules.name: The Instrument-Scale Rule
rules.body: The dashboard's type lives between 11px and 26px, on five sizes. A page title is 15px, not a marketing headline. When something needs emphasis, step up in weight or contrast (Ink 3 → Ink 2 → Ink), not in size. Only the view's one focal figure uses Display.

rules.name: The Machine-String Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is for identifiers a machine emitted or will parse: URLs, model ids, tier names, headers, tags, key fragments, price versions, decision layers and failure kinds. **Numbers are not identifiers.** Money, counts, durations and percentages are Geist with tabular figures everywhere, from readout cells to table rows. Never set prose or figures in Mono.

rules.name: The Literal Breakpoint Rule
rules.body: Breakpoints are literal numbers inside media and container queries, mirrored in `STYLESEED.md`, because `@media (max-width: var(--x))` is invalid and fails silently. Change the stylesheet and the lock together, never one alone.

rules.name: The Class-Not-Inline Rule
rules.body: Any geometry that changes at a breakpoint lives in an `rs-*` class. An inline `style` outranks every class, so a responsive rule aimed at it parses, matches and does nothing. `responsive.test.ts` guards the known sites.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separation is always a 1px border: Hairline around a surface, Soft Hairline inside it. Never use a shadow, a heavier border or a filled band to separate surfaces. Tonal fills mark *state* (hover, selected, a notice), never structure. For example, a group-boundary row in a table is an Overline label above a Soft Hairline, not a filled band. Inset notes and key–value boxes (Canvas fill, 6px radius) are the one structural tone: like inputs, they read as wells cut into the panel.

rules.name: The Dark-Is-Flat Rule
rules.body: In dark mode every shadow token is `none`. Depth comes only from the tonal steps from canvas to panel to chip.

rules.name: The Dashed-Means-Absent Rule
rules.body: A dashed *border* means something is absent. There are three cases: not set up yet (the Setup card), not available on this instance (an unavailable switch), and never contacted (a skipped Route Trace attempt). A solid border means present. In charts, a dashed *line* is a reference line (a threshold or ceiling) or a non-focal series, always labelled directly.

rules.name: The Nested Radius Rule
rules.body: An inner element's radius is its container's radius minus the gap between them. A 6px track with 2px padding holds 4px segments; a 10px toggle track holds an 8px knob. Where the padding is larger than the outer radius (a 10px panel with 16px padding), the inner element simply takes its own role's radius.

rules.name: The Words-Not-Zeros Rule
rules.body: A zero is a measurement. Never use it to mean unknown, loading, failed, unavailable or absent. Each of those has its own words.

rules.name: The One-Dash Rule
rules.body: A lone `—` in a figure slot means *pending* and nothing else. A dash never prefixes or stands in for a state word (`— unpriced` is wrong, `unpriced` is right). Inside a phrase it is ordinary punctuation (`unpriced — cost not tracked`).

dos: **Do** explain traffic with the Route Trace. When a surface answers "where did this go, and why", draw the route in the brand mark's grammar. Don't add another table.
**Do** spend indigo by the Indigo Budget: one indigo-filled control and one indigo data series per view. Indigo text is `accent-deep`, never `--accent`.
**Do** write color as tokens: `var(--accent)` and its `color-mix` derivations, never a hex in a component.
**Do** give every figure slot its states from *Figures and their states*, in words: `· est.`, `unpriced`, `<$0.01`, `$0 · not billed`, `≤ $3.00`, `$1.50 over budget`.
**Do** draw entry controls with Control Edge (3:1+), and show every state by a change in shape, border or weight, never by a tint alone.
**Do** keep every control in the height family (24 / 32px, 44px coarse), and every space on the 4px scale.
**Do** give every pressable control visible hover, pressed, focus and busy states, as tone, border or label changes.
**Do** confirm destructive actions with the resource and the consequence in words, and commit with the red Destructive commit button.
**Do** meet the 24px hit-target floor at every width, and 44px below 768px or under a coarse pointer. Set input text at 16px there.
**Do** put any geometry that changes at a breakpoint in an `rs-*` class. Change `STYLESEED.md`, `styles.css` and the contract tests together, and remove the matching As-built delta row.
donts: **Don't** build a rainbow dashboard: no hue per card, series or category, and no colored stripes or icons used only for identity. Identity is carried by text.

**Don't** slide into enterprise grey sludge. That means heavy or doubled borders, Control Edge on surfaces that aren't controls, text below 11px, text lighter than Ink 3, and screens where every panel has equal weight.
**Don't** use the hero-metric template (big number, small label, supporting stats, accent) as a row of identical cards. Use one Readout strip with one Display figure.
**Don't** let a zero mean unknown, loading, failed, unavailable or absent. Don't pair a dash with a word (`— unpriced`), and don't print an estimate without `· est.`.
**Don't** set figures in Mono, or prose in Mono. Mono is for identifiers.
**Don't** separate surfaces with drop shadows, nest a panel inside a panel, or show any shadow in dark mode. Selected edges are borders, never `box-shadow`.
**Don't** use pure black (#000) text. Ink is #17181a.
**Don't** use amber for an action, or an indigo commit inside a destructive dialog.

**Don't** animate figures, Route Trace paths or page loads. Don't loop anything except the in-progress pulses (running, queued, cancelling, reconciling) and skeletons; the Live lamp blinks only on an event.
**Don't** fetch fonts or assets from a third party, or set a responsive dimension in an inline `style`. An inline style outranks the breakpoint rule and silently ignores it.
